title: Control charts
subtitle: A factory cannot inspect every item — but it can watch the average and notice the moment the process drifts.

sections.title: Two kinds of variation
sections.body: Every process varies. Common-cause variation is the steady random noise of a healthy process; special-cause variation comes from something specific (worn tool, new supplier). Statistical quality control (SQC) separates the two so we act only on real changes.

questions.prompt: A sudden jump after changing supplier is…

responses.title: Close, but not it.
responses.body: A step change is not noise.

sections.title: The X̄ chart
sections.body: Take small samples (size n) regularly and plot each sample mean. Centre line = grand mean X̿. Control limits sit three standard errors away: UCL, LCL = X̿ ± 3σ/√n (or X̿ ± A₂R̄ from tabulated constants). Because P(|Z| ≤ 3) = 0.9973, a healthy process almost never crosses them by chance: about 1 false alarm in 370.

choices.text: Three standard errors from the centre line.

responses.title: A tempting idea.
responses.body: Specs are customer requirements, not process behaviour.

figures.caption: Figure 5.2.1 — monitoring loop
figures.script:
diagram("Process -> Sample n items : every hour
Sample n items -> Plot mean : compute x̄
Plot mean -> Inside limits? : compare to LCL, UCL
Inside limits? -> Continue : yes
Inside limits? -> Investigate cause : no");

problems.prompt: Process mean 100, σ = 6, samples of n = 9. Find the X̄ chart limits.

sections.title: Signals beyond one point
sections.body: A single point outside the limits is one signal. Others: 7 points in a row on one side of the centre line, 6 steadily rising, 2 of 3 beyond 2σ. Each pattern is unlikely under pure noise, so it flags a shift earlier than waiting for the limit.

questions.prompt: Eight consecutive points above the centre line suggest…

responses.title: Close, but not it.
responses.body: It is very unlikely by chance.

sections.title: Charts for attributes
sections.body: For defective fractions use the p-chart: centre p̄, limits p̄ ± 3√(p̄(1 − p̄)/n). For defects per unit use the c-chart: c̄ ± 3√c̄ (Poisson). Lower limits below zero are set to zero.

sections.title: Process capability
sections.body: Control asks “is it stable?”; capability asks “does it meet the spec?” Cp = (USL − LSL)/6σ. Cp ≥ 1.33 is comfortable; Cp = 1 leaves 0.27 % out of spec. Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/3σ also penalises an off-centre mean.

worked.why: So Cp = 1.33 if the mean is centred.

questions.prompt: Cp = 1.33 means the spec width is…

sections.title: Acceptance sampling
sections.body: A single-sampling plan (n, c) inspects n items from a lot and accepts if at most c are defective. The operating-characteristic curve plots P(accept) against the lot defect rate — computed with the binomial (or Poisson). Producer’s risk α rejects a good lot; consumer’s risk β accepts a bad one.

questions.prompt: Plan n = 50, c = 0 versus c = 2. Which accepts more lots?
